title: Technology Sector Update for 05/10/2018: ROKU,BT,HIMX,INFN
text:

Technology stocks rose Thursday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding more than 1.1% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 1.6% gain.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Roku ( ROKU ) was tipping lower in late Thursday trading, erasing a nearly 8% rise soon after today's opening bell, that followed the streaming television service reporting above-consensus Q1 results and forecasting Q2 and FY18 revenue also exceeding Wall Street expectations. Pro forma net loss for the three months ended March 31 narrowed to $0.07 per share from $0.09 per share during the prior-year period and beating the Capital IQ consensus looking for a $0.16 per share net loss. Revenue rose 36% year over year to $136.6 million, also topping the $127.6 million Street view. Roku sees is projecting Q2 revenue in a range of $135 million to $145 million and FY18 revenue between $685 million to $705 million, exceeding the analyst mean expecting $135.3 million in Q2 revenue and $674.7 million in FY18 revenue, respectively.
In other sector news:
(+) Himax Technologies ( HIMX ) was almost 1% higher late Thursday afternoon, with shares of the fabless chipmaker firming after previously see-sawing between small gains and losses in choppy trade that followed it swinging to a Q1 net loss compared with a year-ago profit but still beating Wall Street expectations on the its top and bottom lines. The fabless chipmaker recorded a non-IFRS loss of $0.015 per American depository shares during the three months ended March 31, reversing an adjusted $0.01 per ADS profit during the year-ago period but still topping the Capital IQ consensus looking for an adjusted net loss of $0.03 per ADS. Revenue rose 4.9% year-over-year to $162.9 million, also exceeding the $160.7 million analyst mean.
(-) BT Group ( BT ) slid to its lowest share price since September 2011, dropping over 9% to $14.72 per American depository share, after announcing plans to eliminate up to 13,000 jobs over the next three years as part of a GBP1.5 billion cost-savings program. The consumer electronics and networking services company said the $2.04 billion program will largely target back office and middle management positions and comes in response to a forecast drop in its FY19 revenue and non-GAAP earnings before interest, taxes, depriciation and amortization. The company is projecting a 2% drop in revenue this year from its $32.14 billion in revenue during the 12 months ended March 31. That translates to $31.5 billion versus the two-analyst estimate looking for $33.74 billion in revenue for the current fiscal year.
(-) Infinera ( INFN ) tumbled Thursday, falling as much as 20%, despite narrowing its adjusted Q1 net loss compared with the year-ago period and beating analyst forecasts. Excluding one-time items, the networking equipment company generated a non-GAAP Q1 net loss of $0.05 per share during the three months ended March 31, improving on a $0.15 per share loss last year and exceeding the Capital IQ consensus expecting an adjusted net loss of $0.11 per share. Revenue rose to $202.7 million from $175.5 million last year, also topping the $200.81 million analyst mean.
